subject: Banking
title: Whistleblowers Who Changed Banking
description: A short lesson to help you apply Whistleblowers Who Changed Banking.

hook.text: Bank whistleblowers risked careers, relationships, and safety to expose fraud. One received $104 million.

buildup.text: Bradley Birkenfeld exposed UBS's tax evasion scheme. He went to prison first.

discovery.text: Dodd-Frank created financial rewards for whistleblowers: 10-30% of penalties over $1 million from enforcement.

twist.text: Most whistleblowers still face retaliation. They lose their jobs, get blacklisted from the industry.

climax.text: Whistleblowers are banking's immune system. They detect fraud that regulators miss.

punchline.text: They expose billion-dollar fraud. Some get rewards.

quiz.question: What happened to UBS whistleblower Bradley Birkenfeld?
options: He went to prison first, then received $104 million

details.summary: Banking whistleblowers like Sherron Watkins at Enron, Bradley Birkenfeld at UBS, and Howard Wilkinson at Danske Bank exposed major fraud at personal cost, often facing retaliation before being vindicated years later.
details.whyItMatters: Most banking scandals are discovered by insiders, not regulators. Protecting and incentivizing whistleblowers is one of the most effective tools for detecting fraud before it causes systemic damage.
takeaways: Bradley Birkenfeld received $104 million for exposing UBS tax fraud
Many whistleblowers face career destruction and legal retaliation
The Dodd-Frank Act created SEC bounties for whistleblower tips

faq.question: Are banking whistleblowers adequately protected?
faq.answer: Legally, protections have improved through Dodd-Frank and similar laws. In practice, whistleblowers still routinely face career destruction, blacklisting from the industry, and years of legal battles before receiving any vindication.

faq.question: How much can whistleblowers earn from reporting fraud?
faq.answer: SEC whistleblower awards range from 10 to 30 percent of sanctions exceeding $1 million. Bradley Birkenfeld received $104 million for exposing UBS's tax evasion scheme, the largest whistleblower award in history at the time.
